status: proposed extensions to existing MetaDrive metadata only; this is NOT a parallel persistence model
purpose: Make platform pages and builders consume the same Objects, Actions, Flows and registered Components as tenant applications

authorities.reuse: existing object definitions and generic tenant record API
existing published registered component renderer and sandbox
existing registry resolver, extended surface scope
existing page and layout metadata; add protected system ownership fields
existing metadata bindings and server-authorised Action/Flow execution
existing permission system and platform/tenant boundary
existing installer and additive/idempotent metadata merge
existing metadata state registry, backed by existing persistence

scopes.name: tenant
scopes.writableBy: tenant principals authorised by existing RBAC

resolutionOrder: authenticated tenant context and server-side permission check
published tenant-owned page or permitted system presentation override
fail closed when no authorised definition exists
securityInvariants: The browser never authorises access; server-side RBAC remains authoritative on Objects, fields, records, Actions, Flows and platform operations
A tenant metadata override cannot change platform-only permissions, impersonate a user or bypass tenant isolation
OneEngine permission seeding creates initially editable grants without resetting administrators' subsequent changes
Untrusted custom components stay sandboxed; trustedBundled cannot be set by tenant metadata
Render only published versioned definitions; keep immutable last-known-good system page and secure recovery access
migrationRules: Add compatible metadata fields and migration functions to current data structures; do not invent a second metadata engine
Seed system pages through versioned idempotent package metadata; preserve existing tenant pages and navigation
Run old and new rendering paths behind a reversible compatibility boundary until parity tests pass
Do not remove legacy routes or direct JSX until behaviour, deep links, accessibility, mobile and RBAC parity are verified
Extract cohesive modules by responsibility rather than one-off app handlers or monolithic code
